VISIBLE & EDITABLE

The assumptions behind your result

These are illustrative nominal assumptions, not current market forecasts. Historical evidence uses a separate sourced dataset.

Cash yield can change in practice. Historical Treasury returns include price changes; they are not a guaranteed yield to maturity. VTI uses an S&P 500 historical proxy. Global, international and custom choices have no historical backtest in this version.

Taxes & account access

Verify your own deduction threshold, loan eligibility and remaining contribution room. Defaults are examples, not filing-year limits. State taxes are approximated by combined rates. Gains tax is reserved at the horizon; dividends are taxed during growth. No loss tax credit is assumed.

Traditional and HSA contributions are grossed up for an assumed immediate deduction; excess goes to taxable brokerage. Roth uses after-tax money. Qualified HSA medical withdrawals are tax-free. Locked accounts are excluded from liquidity, without assuming early withdrawals. Employer match, required distributions, early penalties, tax bracket changes, sale timing of lots and tax-law changes are excluded.

TRUST STARTS WITH THE MATH

Follow every dollar

Each strategy starts with the same cash, lump sum and monthly budget: scheduled principal-and-interest payment plus your extra amount. Property tax and insurance continue after payoff, so they are never treated as freed money.

Each month, mortgage interest accrues on the remaining principal. Payments are capped at the amount owed. Extra principal pays down the loan; unused payment money is invested. The cash strategy keeps freed payments in cash. Monthly investing happens at month end. A lump sum is deployed today.

Mortgage tax savings are calculated annually from the additional itemized deduction above your deduction threshold. The refund is added to taxable investments at year end. All assumptions are held fixed over time unless a scenario explicitly changes them.

Mortgage formulas

Monthly payment = B × i / [1 − (1 + i)−n], where B is balance, i is annual note rate / 12, and n is remaining months. At zero interest, payment = B / n.

Balance next month = max(0, balance × (1 + i) − regular payment − extra principal). We retain full precision and round only displayed amounts.

What “robust” means here

The robustness label measures agreement of the invest-versus-mortgage median across all available views and the distance between assumed return and deterministic break-even. “Strong” requires full agreement, each view showing at least 65% of paths favoring the same direction, and a margin over 2 percentage points. It is not a calibrated confidence score.

The most robust allocation minimizes the 90th-percentile regret in the conventional model: the gap from the best allocation in each same market path. This is a specific risk criterion, not a universal definition of the best decision. It differs from maximizing average wealth.

Historical and modeled uncertainty

Historical rolling windows overlap and are not independent observations. Block resampling rearranges three-year blocks and may miss unprecedented events. Lognormal paths can understate extreme events. Regime and starting-condition models are illustrative challenges, not independent calibrated forecasts.

Annual historical returns are converted to a uniform monthly compound rate within each year. Actual monthly timing, changing dividend yields, international currencies and portfolio rebalancing taxes are not represented. Modeled paths reuse a fixed seed so changing an input changes the assumptions rather than random luck.

Supported scope & known limits

This version supports amortizing fixed-rate mortgages, recurring extra payments and lump sums. Home sale and early retirement scenarios stop the comparison at the selected earlier horizon; sale does not forecast a replacement home.

Adjustable rates, PMI removal, refinancing, recasting and contractual prepayment penalties need additional modeling and are not supported. An adjustable-rate selection stops the calculation. Investment selections are broad proxies; ETF expenses, dividend yield and account limits need review. There is no live forecast feed or AI-generated financial arithmetic.
